description: We are Cosmic Bond, a two-person team formed by an Electrical-Electronics Engineering student and a Mechatronics Engineering student. We share a passion for space exploration, science, technology, and innovation. Our strengths include software development, electronics, control systems, automation, simulation, and problem-solving. We combine different engineering perspectives to turn creative ideas into practical solutions. Two minds, one mission, endless possibilities.
summary:
On Mars, a 25-minute round-trip communication delay (RTLT) with Earth makes real-time guidance from Houston impossible during emergencies, while orbital hillshade imagery conceals lethal >28° slopes and >0.38m rock steps from a 120 kg spacesuited astronaut.

COSMIC BOND // ARES-VII is an end-to-end autonomous Marswalk decision support system, co-robotic mission planner, and wearable ESP32 hardware twin built on authentic NASA data for Mount Sharp, Gale Crater.

By fusing a 10,000-node numerical NASA MGS MOLA DEM (23.66 m/cell) with live Mars Trek WMTS layers (MRO HiRISE 0.25m, CTX 6m, Viking MDIM21, Odyssey THEMIS IR), Curiosity GPS track points, and MSL RAD radiation baselines, our white-box physics engine computes Human Walkability Index (HWI) and Data Confidence Score (DCS) under strict "Unknown Terrain != Safe" rules. It solves 3-corridor 8-way TrueGrid A* routes in 4.3 ms, generates Multi-Source Dijkstra Walkback Point-of-No-Return (PNR) contours, locates natural canyon radiation shelters (1.28 min Topographic Defilade vs 10.78 min base return), coordinates 6WD Co-Robotic rover sample handoffs (-21.8% mechanical work), and syncs bi-directionally with our ESP32 J.A.R.V.I.S. Mark VII wrist terminal.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

COSMIC BOND // ARES-VII (Engineered by Sabri Can YURT & Irem Merve YILMAZ) transforms raw planetary remote sensing into deterministic, life-saving EVA decisions across four integrated layers:

• 5-Layer NASA Data Fusion (Visual != Walkable): Strictly separates visual-only basemaps from numerical elevation matrices. Using a 100x100 MGS MOLA DEM patch at Mount Sharp (23.66 m/cell), it computes slope, aspect, step height, and thermal inertia to output a Human Walkability Index (HWI 0-100) and Data Confidence Score (DCS 0-100).

• White-Box Survival Algorithms:

- 8-Way TrueGrid A* (~4.3 ms): Solves 3-corridor routes 376,000x faster than the 25m 04s Earth RTLT delay, with a hard NO_SAFE_WALKABLE_ROUTE safety lock.

- Multi-Source Dijkstra Walkback PNR: Computes real-time Point-of-No-Return (10.78 min) oxygen/fatigue envelopes under Martian gravity (3.71 m/s², 0.378g).

- 3D SVF Topographic Defilade: Identifies natural sandstone cliff alcoves in 1.28 min (8.42x faster than returning to base) during solar radiation storms.

- 1,000-Run Monte Carlo Simulation: Validates 98% survival rate across stochastic dust and radiation crises.

• Co-Robotic Rover & 0/1 Knapsack Triage: Coordinates a 6WD Rocker-Bogie support rover with a 60° LiDAR scanner, reducing astronaut mechanical work by 21.8% and optimizing emergency sample triage (14 kg / 188 pts).

• Orbital OSINT, DSN & ESP32 Hardware Twin: Tracks 5 Mars orbiters (MRO, Odyssey, MAVEN, TGO, Mars Express) and 3 NASA DSN 70m stations (Goldstone, Madrid, Canberra @ 278 dB FSPL), linked bi-directionally to an ESP32-WROOM-32 J.A.R.V.I.S. Mark VII wrist terminal (128x128 ILI9163C TFT, 12x WS2812B compass ring, MPU6050 IMU, Joystick, VOX voice control).

2. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & HARDWARE

• Backend: Python 3, Flask, NumPy.

• Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JS, Leaflet, custom 2D/3D Canvas engines, Web Speech API.

• Hardware Twin: C++ / Arduino (sketch.ino), ESP32-WROOM-32, ILI9163C TFT, WS2812B, MPU6050.

3. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE

Core navigation (A*, Dijkstra PNR, SVF Defilade, HWI/DCS) is 100% deterministic white-box math with zero ML hallucination. Generative SI tools assisted with the first 7 seconds of concept video intro scenes (watermarked) and code/documentation formatting.
